#### 10. Sandhoff disease  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.388)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9840310)

**Proposed mechanism:** GBA2 (HGNC:4079) —DECREASES→ Glucosylceramide (CHEBI:57519); Glucosylceramide (CHEBI:57519) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0005707); Lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0005707) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodegeneration (HP:0002375); HEXB (HGNC:4979) —DECREASES→ GM2-ganglioside (CHEBI:17890); GM2-ganglioside (CHEBI:17890) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0005707); Lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0005707) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263). **How to falsify it:** If genetic evidence demonstrates that mutations in GBA2 or HEXB in patients with MONDO:0013737 or Sandhoff disease, respectively, do not lead to the accumulation of their respective substrates (glucosylceramide or GM2-ganglioside) within lysosomes, or if these patients exhibit normal lysosomal degradation pathway function, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Presence of common variants in GBA2 or HEXB with a minor allele frequency > 1% in relevant gnomAD populations, which are not associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared disruption of the lysosomal degradation pathway offers potential therapeutic avenues. Strategies aimed at enhancing lysosomal function or clearing accumulated substrates could be beneficial for both conditions, despite originating from mutations in different genes.
